name: Roland FA-06/07/08
description: Roland FA-06, FA-07 and FA-08 music workstations (one sound engine, one address map): the setup, the system blocks, the whole temporary Studio Set with its sixteen parts, and Part 1's temporary tone in each of the five tone types it can hold, from the MIDI Implementation.

sources.title: FA-06/07/08 MIDI Implementation (version 1.01, June 1, 2017)
sources.notes: Parameter Address Map read by tools/profiles/roland/parse-address-map.mjs from FA-06_07_08_MIDI_Imple_eng01_W.pdf (sha256 590e55b3dfad1634eb2136516fe166c3eeb6a003dfceb4c008c8fb37b8c05007). Model ID 00 00 77, DT1 = 12, RQ1 = 11, Roland checksum. Not yet checked against the instrument itself.

authoringNotes: Generated by tools/profiles/roland/make-profiles.mjs; edit the layout in tools/profiles/roland/synths/, not this file.
Every parameter is the manual's, at the manual's address, with the manual's name. Nothing here has been sent to a real instrument yet.
One profile for the FA-06, FA-07 and FA-08: the Identity Reply (p9) is the same family 77 02 / 00 00 for all three, and only its software-revision bytes say which (dd = 00 FA-06, 01 FA-08, 02 FA-07).

Model id 00 00 77, as the address map heading (p12), the DT1/RQ1 byte tables (p6, p9) and the worked example (p36) give it. The sentence on p6 ("The model ID … is 00H 00H 64H") and the transmitted DT1's status line on p9 say 64H, which is the INTEGRA-7's model id; the byte tables directly beneath both say 77H.

The Temporary Tone table (p12) names its entries Temporary PCM Tone, Synth Tone, SuperNATURAL Tone, Drum Kit and Rhythm Set without saying which tone table each holds; they are read as PCM Synth Tone (+00 00 00), SuperNATURAL Synth Tone (+01 00 00), SuperNATURAL Acoustic Tone (+02 00 00), SuperNATURAL Drum Kit (+03 00 00) and PCM Drum Kit (+10 00 00), the INTEGRA-7's printed layout.
Zone n (Studio Set Zone) is filed under Part n: the manual numbers the sixteen zones as it numbers the sixteen parts.

Seven rows are printed with a range and no name, and keep the id the generator gives a nameless row: System Common 00 06 (0-1, system.value), TFX 00 02-00 05 (0-127 each, tfx.value and tfx.value_<address>), Studio Set Common 00 34 (0-15, studioSet.value) and Studio Set Controller 00 18 (0-15, controller.value).

coverage.inboundControllers: not modelled: what the front panel transmits (Control Change, p7-9) is not mapped yet
coverage.parts: the Studio Set's Part, Part EQ, Zone and Part 2 (MKB) blocks for all sixteen parts; the temporary TONE for Part 1 only, in all five types. Parts 2-16's temporary tones are not laid out: Temporary Tone (Studio Mode Part n) is at 19 00 00 00 + (n-1) x 00 20 00 00 (19 20 00 00, 19 40 00 00, 19 60 00 00, 1A 00 00 00 … 1C 60 00 00), with the same five tone types at the same offsets inside it
coverage.pcmDrumKitKeys: PCM drum kit partials for keys 35-81 (the General MIDI percussion keys) only. The map has keys 21-108: partial (Key # k) is at the part's tone base + 10 00 00 + 00 10 00 + (k-21) x 00 02 00, so for Part 1 keys 21-34 are at 19 10 10 00-19 10 2A 00 and keys 82-108 at 19 11 0A 00-19 11 3E 00; all eighty-eight would be 12,672 parameters
coverage.toneTypes: a part plays one tone type at a time; the blocks of the other four types are laid out at their addresses, but the manual does not say what the instrument does with a write or a request to a type the part is not playing. It does say (p6) that a request it cannot answer gets no reply, and the startup pull asks for all five types in turn, so on hardware the pull may stop at the first tone type Part 1 is not playing
coverage.effectParameterMeanings: type-dependent: MFX, IFX, TFX, chorus and reverb parameters are Roland's 4-nibble container (12768-52768, shown -20000..+20000); what each slot does depends on the selected type, which the MIDI Implementation does not list
